# FuelSense

> Fuel intelligence for Nigerian fleets. FuelSense turns Teltonika GPS tracker
> telemetry into auditable fuel cost: distance driven, engine hours, idling
> time, fuel burned and what all of it cost in naira.

FuelSense is a web application for fleet managers, built for Nigerian
operating conditions. It works with the Teltonika FMC150 tracker and does not
require a fuel-level sensor, a CAN adapter or any modification to the fuel
system.

## How it measures fuel without a fuel sensor

The FMC150 computes fuel consumption in its own firmware from satellite-
measured movement and a configured consumption profile, and reports it as two
AVL elements:

- AVL 12, Fuel Used GPS: a running total of millilitres burned, which resets
  when the device loses power.
- AVL 13, Fuel Rate GPS: the instantaneous burn rate in litres per hour.

FuelSense keeps a per-vehicle virtual tank that drains against AVL 12, is
credited by fuel receipts drivers upload, and is priced at the fuel price in
force on the day the fuel was burned. Because both AVL elements are firmware
estimates rather than measurements, FuelSense continuously cross-checks them
against each other and calibrates the result against litres actually paid for,
then reports a confidence figure instead of claiming certainty.

## What it does not claim

FuelSense cannot see fuel being siphoned from a tank, because without a
fuel-level sensor or CAN bus connection no such measurement exists. What it
reports instead is a discrepancy: where litres purchased on receipts do not
match the burn measured from the vehicle's movement, it raises the gap as a
question for a manager to investigate, never as an accusation.

## Main capabilities

- Live map tracking with trips segmented automatically from ignition state
- Stop detection with reverse-geocoded addresses
- Idling measured to the minute and priced in naira
- Fuel consumption and cost per kilometre against realistic benchmarks for
  Nigerian city driving
- Driver receipt upload with OCR, reconciled against measured burn
- Effective-dated fuel pricing, so past periods keep the price that applied
  when the fuel was burned
- Driving behaviour events: harsh braking, acceleration, cornering, overspeed
- Email alerts for low fuel, trip starts and tracker tampering

## Realistic efficiency benchmarks used

Measured for Nigerian city conditions with air conditioning running, not
manufacturer combined-cycle figures:

- Toyota Corolla: 8 to 10 km/L
- Toyota Camry: 7 to 9 km/L
- Toyota RAV4: 6 to 8 km/L
- Toyota Hilux: 6 to 8 km/L
- Toyota Hiace: 5.5 to 7 km/L
